I found two trailing-antonym clauses in the passage.

1. "Access checks default to fail-closed, rather than open." The trailer "rather than open" names the ordinary antonym of "closed". Anyone would know it, so I cut it.

2. "Those privilege limits are imposed on purpose, rather than by accident." This matches the rule's own example of on purpose/by accident, so I cut it.

I left the other negation phrases alone. "Not merely an IT concern" in the conclusion is a leading "not merely", not a trailing clause. "Rather than exploit them" in the bug-bounty sentence is a genuine behavioral contrast, not an ordinary antonym of "report". It sits inside the sentence and describes what the incentive steers away from, so it needs no change under this rule.
